title: T5 Compositor Interview
eyebrow: GUI.Forms · stage T5 · compositor cooperation · interview round 1
lede: T5 lets windows cooperate with the desktop’s compositor: transparency and the system’s frosted materials, plus full-fidelity glass and reflection. The plan is in planning/stages/T5-compositor/PLAN.md (PR #321). Section A holds the decisions that are yours; section B holds platform calls where I would accept the plan’s recommendations. Your answers are kept in this browser; save them to a file or copy the record back to the coordinating session.
context_html:
Where T5 stands

The engine half is built: glass inside a window blurs a cached image of the window’s own background (T2, E9.3). The host half is the plan’s nine phases, C0 to C8, about 16 to 17 PRs: per host, Windows DWM (client alpha; Mica and Acrylic from Windows 11 22H2), macOS visual effect views (14.0), X11 ARGB visuals with and without a compositor, and Wayland as a note. Every capability is reported honestly per host, and a window always falls back without an error.

Three things still need measuring on real systems, whatever you choose: which Windows route gives clean transparency with the native title bar, the 32-bit visual under Xvfb, and compositor detection under XWayland.
footer_html: They become owner decisions in planning/stages/T5-compositor/README.md, and the T5 worker builds the phases in order, each as its own PR with its gate.
